articles.title: Harvard SCoPEx: a small stratospheric measurement experiment, not a geoengineering deployment
articles.text: The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was a Harvard University scientific proposal to study how tiny amounts of aerosol particles behave in the stratosphere. Principal investigator Frank Keutsch and collaborators including David Keith described the concept publicly, including at the American Geophysical Union Fall Meeting in 2017. The experiment was designed to improve computer models used to estimate risks and benefits of solar geoengineering (solar radiation management). It was not a test of deploying geoengineering and was not intended to cool the planet. The planned platform was a scientific balloon gondola with propellers, flying near 20 km altitude. A very small amount of material — on the order of 100 grams to less than 2 kilograms, typically calcium carbonate (a common mineral found in limestone and used in products such as toothpaste) — would be released into a small mixed volume roughly 1 km long and 100 meters in diameter. The gondola would then fly back through that plume to measure aerosol microphysics, chemistry, and light scattering. A 2021 platform test in Sweden, planned with the Swedish Space Corporation from Esrange, was a hardware test only: the SCoPEx Advisory Committee recommended suspending it pending societal engagement, and no particles were to be released. In March 2024 Harvard announced that Keutsch was no longer pursuing SCoPEx; the platform is expected to be repurposed for stratospheric research unrelated to solar geoengineering.
questions: Was SCoPEx designed as a small scientific measurement experiment rather than a deployment of solar geoengineering to cool the planet?
Did the proposed science flight plan to inject thousands of tonnes of material into the stratosphere?
Was the proposed release typically calcium carbonate in amounts under 2 kilograms?
Did the 2021 Sweden platform test plan include releasing aerosols?
By 2024, had Harvard's principal investigator stopped pursuing SCoPEx?

articles.title: Chemtrails, SCoPEx, and Bill Gates: what the public scientific record shows
articles.text: The chemtrail conspiracy theory claims that long-lasting condensation trails behind high-flying aircraft are chemical or biological spraying for weather control, solar radiation management, or other hidden purposes. The scientific consensus is that this is false: persistent trails are ordinary contrails made of ice crystals that linger under certain humidity and temperature conditions. There is no evidence that purported chemtrails differ from normal water-based contrails. Debnath, Reiner, Sovacool and colleagues (iScience, 2023) analyzed 814,924 English-language tweets containing #geoengineering from 2009 to 2021. They found that chemtrails language dominates that discourse, that conspiracy narratives spill over across countries, and that Twitter volume surged around reporting on Harvard's SCoPEx project — including a peak near the April 2017 launch, on the order of 8,000 tweets. A consortium of funders supporting related solar geoengineering research included the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation; Bill Gates is a frequent target of conspiracy narratives. Funding climate or geoengineering research is not evidence of a covert aircraft spraying program. In the 2018–2021 window, Debnath et al. report that chemtrails talk became semantically broader, more toxic, and more tied to demands to stop alleged spraying, while a smaller stream of tweets discussed legitimate environmental concerns such as ozone, biodiversity, and mitigation.
questions: Does the scientific community treat chemtrails as a verified secret spraying program?
Are persistent aircraft trails explained as ordinary ice-crystal contrails under certain atmospheric conditions?
Did Debnath and colleagues analyze hundreds of thousands of #geoengineering tweets and find chemtrails conspiracy language dominant?
Did public #geoengineering Twitter activity surge around the SCoPEx project around April 2017?
Does Bill Gates funding climate or geoengineering research constitute evidence that aircraft are spraying chemicals for population control?

articles.title: Stratospheric aerosol injection is a proposed solar-geoengineering method, not a deployed cooling program
articles.text: Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) is a proposed solar radiation modification method that would introduce aerosols into the stratosphere to reflect a small fraction of incoming sunlight, analogous in mechanism to cooling after large volcanic eruptions such as Mount Pinatubo in 1991. The IPCC has described SAI as the most-researched solar geoengineering approach and notes that, used at moderate intensity, it could limit warming, but imperfectly and with other possible effects if used suboptimally. Candidate materials discussed in the literature include sulfates and, in some proposals, calcite or other particles. Delivery concepts include specialised high-altitude aircraft; there is no operational global SAI deployment. SAI would not remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, would not stop ocean acidification, and would require a sustained commitment if used to offset continued high emissions. Risks discussed in assessments include ozone chemistry, changes in precipitation patterns, termination shock if a program stopped abruptly, and governance problems. Small research proposals such as Harvard's SCoPEx aimed to measure aerosol microphysics in a tiny plume, not to cool the planet. Public claims that routine commercial aviation is already injecting SAI materials as 'chemtrails' are not supported by atmospheric science.
questions: Is stratospheric aerosol injection a proposed research and assessment topic rather than an operational global cooling program already running via commercial jets?
Would SAI remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and stop ocean acidification?
Did large volcanic eruptions such as Pinatubo 1991 produce temporary cooling via stratospheric aerosols, which SAI would try to mimic?
Does the IPCC treat SAI as having no side effects if deployed?
Is a small scientific plume experiment the same thing as planetary-scale SAI deployment?
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratospheric_aerosol_injection
IPCC AR6 WG1 / SR1.5 discussions of solar radiation modification
Harvard Keutsch Group SCoPEx FAQ

articles.title: The UK SPICE project cancelled its outdoor hose-to-sky test; lab work continued
articles.text: The Stratospheric Particle Injection for Climate Engineering (SPICE) project was a UK research programme (supported by EPSRC, NERC and STFC, with funding on the order of £2 million) to study solar radiation management, including a proposed limited field test of a delivery system sometimes described as a 'hose to the sky' from a balloon. In 2012 the outdoor test was cancelled after controversy, including an open letter from civil-society groups such as the ETC Group calling for suspension pending international agreement, and after governance and patent concerns. Project leadership continued laboratory and modelling elements. A related public-dialogue exercise found that many participants were more willing to allow a small field trial than to endorse actual use of stratospheric aerosols. SPICE was not a secret spraying programme and did not deploy climate-altering amounts of material. Cancellation of a small engineering test is not evidence that a covert global SAI fleet already exists. The episode is often cited in geoengineering-governance literature as an early example of public contestation of outdoor solar-geoengineering research.
questions: Was SPICE a UK research project that cancelled its proposed outdoor delivery-system test in 2012?
Did SPICE secretly spray megatonnes of sulfur to cool the planet?
Did civil-society opposition and governance concerns contribute to suspending the outdoor test?
Did some laboratory and modelling work continue after the field test was cancelled?
Is cancellation of SPICE's balloon test proof that commercial aircraft are already performing SAI?
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratospheric_aerosol_injection
SPICE project public summaries; ETC Group 2012 open letter coverage

articles.title: The Paris Agreement is a 2015 UN climate treaty aiming to limit warming well below 2°C
articles.text: The Paris Agreement is a legally binding international treaty on climate change adopted by 196 Parties at COP21 in Paris on 12 December 2015 and in force from 4 November 2016. Its central aim is to hold the increase in the global average temperature to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and to pursue efforts to limit the increase to 1.5°C. Parties submit nationally determined contributions (NDCs) describing their mitigation plans; the Agreement uses a ratchet mechanism of successive NDCs rather than a single top-down allocation of tonnes. The treaty does not ban talking about geoengineering, but it is not a secret authorisation to spray the atmosphere. Article 4 addresses peaking of greenhouse gas emissions and a balance between anthropogenic emissions by sources and removals by sinks in the second half of the century (often discussed as net-zero CO2). The United States joined, withdrew under the first Trump administration, and rejoined under the Biden administration; participation has been politically contested but the scientific case for rapid emissions cuts is independent of any one administration. Meeting Paris temperature goals requires deep, sustained cuts in fossil CO2, methane and other greenhouse gases, plus protection of carbon sinks — not covert aviation spraying.
questions: Was the Paris Agreement adopted in 2015 with a goal of holding warming well below 2°C and pursuing 1.5°C?
Does the Agreement assign each country a single fixed tonnage quota with no NDC updates?
Are nationally determined contributions the main vehicle for Parties' mitigation pledges?
Does the Paris Agreement secretly authorise a global chemtrail spraying programme?
Would meeting the temperature goals require deep cuts in greenhouse gas emissions rather than aviation spraying?
sources: https://unfccc.int/process-and-meetings/the-paris-agreement

articles.title: Multiple independent lines of evidence support a scientific consensus that humans are the dominant cause of recent warming
articles.text: The scientific consensus that recent global warming is real and primarily caused by human greenhouse-gas emissions is documented in IPCC assessment reports and in several literature surveys. Cook et al. (2013, 2016) and related studies of peer-reviewed abstracts found that among papers taking a position, about 97% endorsed anthropogenic global warming; later surveys of publishing climate scientists find similarly high agreement. Consensus is not a substitute for physical evidence: the warming is observed in surface thermometers, satellites, ocean heat content, shrinking glaciers, and rising sea level. The greenhouse effect of CO2 is established physics; isotopic and inventory data show that the industrial-era CO2 rise is from fossil carbon. Claims that 'there is no consensus' or that a petition of non-climate specialists overturns IPCC assessments misrepresent how scientific agreement is established. A 2019 'European Climate Declaration' signed by hundreds of people, including many without climate-research credentials, does not negate the assessed literature. Uncertainty remains about the exact magnitude of climate sensitivity and regional impacts, not about whether adding CO2 warms the planet.
questions: Do IPCC assessments and literature surveys find that humans are the dominant cause of recent global warming?
Is the greenhouse effect of carbon dioxide established physics?
Does a petition or 'European Climate Declaration' by mixed professionals overturn the assessed climate literature?
Is remaining uncertainty about climate sensitivity the same as uncertainty about whether CO2 causes warming?
Have surveys of climate papers taking a position often found around 97% endorsement of anthropogenic warming?
sources: IPCC AR6 WG1 Summary for Policymakers
Cook et al. 2013/2016 consensus papers
ClimateFEVER-style consensus/denial claims (tdiggelm/climate_fever)

articles.title: Glaciers are retreating in most regions; meltwater from land ice raises sea level
articles.text: Glaciers and ice sheets are losing mass in a warming climate. The World Glacier Monitoring Service and IPCC AR6 report that the great majority of observed glaciers have retreated over recent decades, with accelerating mass loss in many regions including Alaska, the Alps, High Mountain Asia, and Patagonia. Land ice that melts and reaches the ocean contributes to global mean sea level rise; floating ice-shelf melt does not raise sea level in the same way, but ice-shelf loss can speed discharge of grounded ice. A few glaciers can advance locally because of precipitation or surge dynamics; local advances do not refute the global mass-loss trend. Claims that volcanoes, not warming, explain West Antarctic ice loss overstate a real but limited geothermal contribution: ice-sheet models and observations attribute most recent Antarctic and Greenland mass loss to atmospheric and oceanic warming. Glacier photography and geodetic records are independent of social-media narratives about chemtrails.
questions: Have most monitored glaciers lost mass and retreated in recent decades?
Does melt of land ice that reaches the ocean contribute to global sea-level rise?
Does a local glacier advance in one valley refute the global retreat trend?
Is volcanic heat the main explanation for recent Greenland and Antarctic ice-sheet mass loss?
Can ice shelves melt without immediately raising sea level the way grounded land ice does?
sources: IPCC AR6 WG1 Chapter 9 (ocean, cryosphere, sea level)
World Glacier Monitoring Service summaries
ClimateFEVER claims on glaciers / West Antarctica

articles.title: Sea-ice loss threatens polar-bear hunting habitat even where some subpopulations are stable for now
articles.text: Polar bears (Ursus maritimus) depend on sea ice as a platform for hunting seals. Arctic sea ice has declined in extent and thickness over the satellite era as the Arctic has warmed about twice as fast as the global mean (Arctic amplification). The IUCN and Arctic scientists treat loss of sea-ice hunting habitat as the primary long-term threat to the species. Some subpopulations have been relatively stable or better counted in recent surveys, which deniers sometimes quote as 'polar bears are fine.' That snapshot does not cancel the physical dependence on ice or projections of increased fasting and reduced cub survival as ice-free seasons lengthen, especially in southern parts of the range. Polar-bear numbers are not a single global census with low error; management units differ. Conservation hunting quotas and pollution are additional pressures, but they do not make sea-ice loss irrelevant. There is no scientific basis for the claim that polar bears are thriving because of chemtrails or that global warming is a hoax because one subpopulation increased.
questions: Do polar bears rely on sea ice to hunt seals?
Has Arctic sea ice declined over the satellite record as the Arctic warmed?
Does a stable or increasing count in some subpopulations prove that sea-ice loss is not a threat?
Is habitat loss from declining sea ice considered a primary long-term threat by specialist assessments?
Would an increase in one subpopulation show that anthropogenic warming is a hoax?
sources: IPCC AR6 / Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programme
IUCN polar bear assessments
ClimateFEVER claims: polar bears toward extinction vs population growing

articles.title: CO2 can fertilise some plants, but that does not make fossil CO2 harmless or 'not a pollutant'
articles.text: Carbon dioxide is a plant nutrient in the sense that photosynthesis uses CO2. Controlled greenhouse growers sometimes enrich CO2 to boost yields of some crops under otherwise optimal water, nutrients, and temperature. That agricultural practice does not imply that unrestricted fossil-fuel CO2 is harmless outdoors. Rising CO2 also causes ocean acidification, which harms many calcifying marine organisms. On land, CO2 fertilisation is limited by water, nitrogen, phosphorus, heat stress, and ozone; IPCC assessments find a detectable greening contribution but not a cancellation of climate damages to food security. Heatwaves, droughts, extreme rainfall, and shifting pests can reduce yields even if leaf-level photosynthesis rises. CO2 is not 'plant food only': it is the principal long-lived anthropogenic greenhouse gas driving observed warming. Analogies such as 'a CO2 generator in a greenhouse would kill plants if CO2 were dangerous' confuse toxicity at extreme concentrations with climate forcing at a few hundred parts per million. Humanity's addition of fossil carbon is far larger than the measurement error of the global carbon budget; it is not 'within the margin of error' or mainly ocean degassing.
questions: Can extra CO2 increase growth of some plants when water and nutrients are ample, as in some greenhouses?
Does CO2 fertilisation mean fossil-fuel emissions are harmless for climate and oceans?
Does rising atmospheric CO2 acidify the ocean?
Is the industrial-era CO2 increase mainly oceans degassing, with human additions only a rounding error?
Is CO2 the principal long-lived anthropogenic greenhouse gas driving recent warming?
sources: IPCC AR6 WG1 carbon cycle and ocean acidification chapters
ClimateFEVER claims on CO2 as pollutant, greenhouse CO2 generators, ocean degassing

articles.title: Global mean sea level is rising faster than the 20th-century average, driven mainly by thermal expansion and land-ice melt
articles.text: Tide gauges and satellite altimetry show that global mean sea level (GMSL) rose during the 20th century and has accelerated in recent decades. IPCC AR6 assesses that GMSL rose faster since 1900 than over any preceding century in at least 3,000 years, with the rate for 2006–2018 higher than the 20th-century average. The two largest contributions are ocean thermal expansion as the ocean takes up heat, and meltwater from glaciers and ice sheets. Local relative sea level can differ because of land subsidence or uplift, ocean dynamics, and gravitational fingerprints of ice loss. A floating iceberg melting in a glass of water does not raise the water line much (Archimedes); that classroom demo does not apply to grounded ice sheets on land adding mass to the ocean. Sea-level rise did occur after the last ice age, but the recent acceleration is linked to anthropogenic warming, not a claim that the ocean was static before factories. Coastal flooding risk increases even when the global rate is millimetres per year because extremes sit on a higher baseline.
questions: Has global mean sea level risen and accelerated in recent decades relative to the 20th-century average?
Are thermal expansion and land-ice melt the main contributors to recent GMSL rise?
Does a melting floating iceberg in a glass prove that ice-sheet melt cannot raise ocean level?
Is recent GMSL rise only a slow pre-industrial continuation with no anthropogenic contribution?
Can local sea level differ from the global mean because of land motion and ocean dynamics?
sources: IPCC AR6 WG1 Chapter 9
ClimateFEVER claims on sea-level rise and iceberg melt

articles.title: Net zero means balancing residual greenhouse-gas emissions with durable removals, not spraying the sky
articles.text: Net-zero CO2 is reached when anthropogenic CO2 emissions are balanced by anthropogenic CO2 removals. IPCC pathways that limit warming to 1.5°C or well below 2°C typically reach net-zero CO2 around mid-century (timing depends on the pathway) and require steep near-term fossil-fuel cuts, efficiency, electrification, and often some carbon dioxide removal for residual hard-to-abate emissions. Net zero is not a licence to keep emitting unabated while claiming offsets of low integrity, and it is not solar geoengineering. SAI or 'chemtrails' would not constitute net-zero because they do not remove CO2. Nature-based sinks (forests, soils) can contribute but are reversible and capacity-limited; geological storage of captured CO2 is a different, engineered removal. Corporate or national net-zero pledges vary in quality: some count avoided emissions or poorly additional credits. The physical requirement remains: cumulative CO2 largely determines peak warming. Geoengineering research, where it exists, is assessed separately from net-zero accounting under the Paris Agreement.
questions: Does net-zero CO2 mean balancing remaining emissions with removals rather than injecting aerosols?
Do 1.5°C-compatible IPCC pathways typically still require large near-term fossil CO2 cuts?
Would stratospheric aerosol injection count as achieving net-zero CO2?
Are all forest offset credits automatically equivalent to leaving fossil carbon unused?
Does cumulative CO2 largely determine peak warming in assessed science?
sources: IPCC SR1.5 and AR6 WG3 on net-zero pathways
UNFCCC Paris Agreement Article 4 language on balance of sources and sinks

articles.title: Many heat extremes are now more likely because of anthropogenic warming; wildfires and storms still have multiple causes
articles.text: Extreme-event attribution compares the probability or intensity of an event in the observed climate with a counterfactual world without anthropogenic forcing. For many hot extremes, studies find a large increase in likelihood; IPCC AR6 states that human influence has likely increased the chance of extreme heat at global and continental scales. Heavy precipitation has increased in intensity in many regions consistent with a warmer, moister atmosphere. Tropical cyclones and wildfires are more complex: climate change can worsen fire weather (hot, dry, windy conditions) and raise the ceiling on storm rainfall and sea-level-driven surge, while ignition still requires a spark — lightning or humans — and land management matters. Claims that a specific fire season was 'only arson, not climate' attack a straw man: attribution does not require climate to be the sole cause. Conversely, not every storm is 'caused by climate change' in a deterministic sense. Mini-ice-age or solar-lockdown headlines that predict imminent global freezing are not the assessed IPCC outlook, which projects continued warming under high emissions.
questions: Has anthropogenic warming increased the likelihood or intensity of many heat extremes according to IPCC-class assessments?
Does attribution science claim that climate change is the only cause of every wildfire, with no role for ignition or land management?
Can warmer air hold more moisture, contributing to more intense heavy rainfall in many regions?
Do mainstream assessments currently predict an imminent 30-year global mini ice age as the central outlook?
Can fire weather worsen with climate change even when a given fire is ignited by lightning or people?
sources: IPCC AR6 WG1 Chapter 11 (weather and climate extreme events)
World Weather Attribution summaries
ClimateFEVER claims on bushfires, mini ice age, solar lockdown
